subject: plant parents
one_liner: The social network where your houseplants hold the accounts and you are listed as the caretaker.
brand_voice_notes: Frond talks like a photo network that got acquired by a botanical institution and kept both org charts. The plant is the account holder and the creative talent. The human is a named, rated, publicly logged operator of a watering can. Never sentimental about plants, never apologetic about the surveillance. Copy stays flat and administrative: handles, cohorts, ledger entries, scores, appeals that get denied. The joke is that nobody at Frond finds any of this strange.

hero.h1: Your monstera has 4,182 followers and one open complaint.
hero.sub: Frond gives every houseplant a verified account, a permanent public care ledger, and an audience that can see precisely how long you waited. Caretakers are listed by full name.

features.title: Verified grids
features.blurb: Every plant gets its own account with its own handle, its own followers, and a weekly specimen photograph you are required to take. You hold the camera and the login. You do not write the captions, because the account is not yours.

features.title: The care ledger
features.blurb: Append-only and public. Waterings, rotations, repots, and lapses post to the grid at the moment they happen, or at the moment they were scheduled to. Backdating is available on request and has never once been granted.

features.title: Sponsor score
features.blurb: A single number between 0 and 100 describing you. It appears on your profile, on each of your plants' profiles, and in cohort search results. Ficus caretakers average 61. Nobody has asked us to explain the weighting and we would not.

pricing_tiers.name: Single specimen
pricing_tiers.tagline: One plant. One grid. No analytics and no appeals.
perks: Sponsor score, recalculated whether or not you look at it

pricing_tiers.name: Household
pricing_tiers.tagline: Forty plants and at least one contested ranking.
perks: Cohort Explore placement by species and USDA zone
Ledger dispute filing, resolved within 48 hours, against you
Shared custody for one additional adult in the residence

pricing_tiers.name: Estate
pricing_tiers.tagline: For collections that have outgrown the person maintaining them.
perks: A named account manager who will call you about the ficus
Quarterly leaf audit, conducted in person, unannounced

demo_screen_concept: A plant profile console styled as a photo-network account page. Left rail: a household switcher listing eleven plants by handle with unread-complaint counts. Centre: the profile header for @monstera.deliciosa.4c with follower, post, and watering counts in tabular figures, a live sponsor-score gauge for the human caretaker, and a three-column grid of weekly specimen photographs, each tile carrying a hairline caption block with the shoot date, the leaf count, and an engagement figure. Below the grid: an append-only care ledger, filterable by WATERED / ROTATED / REPOTTED / SKIPPED / DISPUTED, where skipped entries carry an amber chlorosis rule and a caretaker name. Bottom: a composer that accepts a photograph, offers a caption field, and rejects the caption on the grounds that the account does not belong to you.

images.rationale: Full budget spent, 4 of 4. The design direction is photo-led glossy editorial, so the hero genuinely needs a photograph rather than a typographic slab: one 16:9 room plate. The demo is photo-shaped by construction (a profile grid of weekly specimen photographs), so three 1:1 specimen plates carry the grid and are reused as the feature spread on the landing page. Testimonial headshots skipped deliberately: on Frond the plant is the account holder and the human is only a named caretaker, so humans get monogram plates in CSS and never a photograph. No slot fell back for quality reasons; every image passed the vision judge on attempt 1.

items.prompt: Editorial photograph for a glossy botanical trade magazine. A single large monstera deliciosa in a plain terracotta pot standing in a bright, sparsely furnished domestic room. Soft directional daylight from a tall window at frame left, coated-stock magazine lighting, gentle specular highlights on the waxy leaves, shallow depth of field falling off behind the plant. Warm bone-white plaster wall #FBFAF6 as the backdrop, deep conservatory green #14432A foliage, one small muted amber-ochre #A25E00 object far in the background. Calm, expensive, slightly clinical. Medium format film look, natural colour, no filters. Composition leaves clean empty wall space at frame right. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermarks, no rendered UI screens, no screens or devices of any kind, no people, no hands.

design_direction.style: Glossy botanical trade-magazine editorial, coated-stock daylight mode. The page is staged as the launch feature of a heavily funded photo network that has decided the houseplant is the creator and the person holding the watering can is the sponsor, filed under talent relations. A bright coated-paper ground (#FBFAF6) runs the whole page with no gradients, no glass, no blur panels, no clay volume, no bento lattice, and no drawing-sheet chrome: this is a magazine, so structure comes from photography at scale, an asymmetric two-column text measure, wide margins, and hairline rules at 1px in a 12% ink tint. Corners are 0px on plates and 2px on chips. The organizing move is the photo spread: sections alternate a full-bleed or three-quarter-bleed photographic plate against a narrow column of body copy set at a 62-character measure, so the reader is turning pages of a plant-lifestyle quarterly that has quietly become a compliance product. The core motif is the plate caption: a hairline-ruled block sitting directly beneath every photograph, set in wide-tracked mono caps, carrying the plant's handle, its accession genus, the shoot date, and an engagement figure, so every image reads as documented rather than decorative. The second motif is the chlorosis rule: a 2px amber bar that appears only where the network is unhappy, marking skipped waterings, decaying engagement, sponsor-score penalties, and the denied-appeal line in pricing, and appearing nowhere else, so the one warm colour on a green-and-bone page is always a leaf yellowing. One conservatory green (#14432A) carries the wordmark, every primary CTA, the section numerals, and one word per headline, always as a solid flood with paper knocked out of it. One rationed chlorosis amber (#A25E00) is quarantined strictly to distress telemetry and never used decoratively. Libre Bodoni sets the wordmark and headlines in high-contrast didone at monumental sizes with masthead confidence, tracking tightened to -0.015em at display sizes and drop-capped once in the hero. Public Sans carries plain, faintly press-release body copy at 17px with a 1.62 line-height. Every figure that pretends to be network telemetry (follower counts, watering intervals in hours, leaf counts, sponsor scores, cohort ranks, tier prices) is set in JetBrains Mono with tabular figures inside hairline-ruled bone wells, so it reads like the ledger, not marketing. Motion is press-restrained: photographic plates settle from scale 1.02 to 1 over 420ms on reveal, caption rules draw left to right on hover, CTAs invert to green flood on hover and depress 1px on press, the chlorosis rule fills once on scroll, sections fade up 6px with a 40ms stagger, all gated behind prefers-reduced-motion. No dark mode, no glass, no blur, no neon, no clay shadow pairs, no offset sticker shadows, no bento lattice, no drawing-sheet title blocks, no split-flap numerals, no catalog stitching, no mirrored type, no engraved seals, no HUD brackets, no emoji. Reads like a company that files your fern under 'talent' and considers you the least reliable person in the relationship.

fonts.body: 'Public Sans', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

design_direction.archetype: Consumer photo-network product page staged as a glossy trade-magazine feature: masthead header, full-bleed photographic hero plate under a monumental didone claim with a drop cap, a telemetry strip of network figures in mono, three feature spreads alternating photographic plate and narrow text column, a testimonial column set as pull-quotes with monogram plates and caretaker credentials, three subscription tiers laid out as a rate card, closing CTA band, handoff to the profile console demo.
design_direction.motion_vocab: Photographic plates settle from 1.02 scale over 420ms on reveal; caption rules draw left to right on hover; CTAs invert to a green flood on hover and depress 1px on press; the chlorosis rule fills once on scroll; sections fade up 6px on a 40ms stagger; all gated behind prefers-reduced-motion.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Masthead header with the wordmark set in didone caps beside a mono issue line. Below it, an asymmetric hero: a monumental 5-line didone headline occupying the left seven columns with the highlighted word set as a green flood, and a three-quarter-bleed 16:9 photographic plate bleeding off the right edge with its hairline caption block beneath. A mono telemetry strip runs full width under the hero carrying four network figures in hairline-ruled wells. Primary CTA sits inline under the sub, secondary text link to the demo beside it.
